react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on two tightly linked amino-acid metabolic modules as the dominant biological signal in this dataset. The foremost cross-paradigm winner is the glycine–serine–threonine metabolism hub (KEGG:map00260 / MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism / KEGG:hsa00260), which ranks #1 in run_ramp_enrichment (FDR = 8.6 × 10⁻¹⁷, 7 of 10 inputs overlapping) and #1 in mummichog (p = 0.0025, 4 input compounds mapping to a compact 8-member module), and #2 in run_metaboanalystr_psea (p = 3.3 × 10⁻⁷, 5 hits). The second consensus module is methionine and cysteine metabolism, detected by run_ramp_enrichment as KEGG:map00270 (FDR = 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁴, 6 hits), by run_metaboanalystr_psea as KEGG:hsa00270 (p = 6 × 10⁻⁴, 3 hits), and by mummichog as the top-2 network module (p = 0.012, 6 hits). These two modules are metabolically linked: L-serine (C00065) sits at the intersection, serving as a substrate for cysteine biosynthesis (via CBS and CGL) and as a one-carbon donor that feeds into the folate pool shared with S-adenosylmethionine. Driver metabolites driving the glycine–serine cluster include glycine (C00037), L-serine (C00065), L-threonine (C00188), and choline (C00114); the methionine/cysteine cluster is anchored by S-adenosylmethionine (C00019) and adenosine (C00212, the adenine moiety that recycles after SAM-dependent methylation). 3,4-Dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043 / CHEBI:27978) is independently picked up by mummichog in the tyrosine metabolism module (rank 6, p = 0.050), indicating a peripheral catecholaldehyde flux. The consistent cross-tool hit on KEGG:hsa00670 (One carbon pool by folate) as top-1 in run_metaboanalystr_psea (p = 8.4 × 10⁻¹⁰) reinforces that one-carbon metabolism — sustained by glycine, serine, and SAM — is the biological narrative unifying the treatment effect.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on amino-acid metabolic pathways as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies KEGG:map00260 Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism as the top hit (FDR = 8.59 × 10⁻¹⁷, fold enrichment 737.4, 7 metabolites hit), with SMPDB Methionine Metabolism (FDR = 1.51 × 10⁻¹⁵, 6 metabolites hit) and KEGG:map00270 Methionine Metabolism (FDR = 1.05 × 10⁻¹⁴, 6 metabolites hit) as strong secondary signals. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00670 One carbon pool by folate (p = 8.36 × 10⁻¹⁰, 6 metabolites hit) and KEGG:hsa00260 Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (p = 3.33 × 10⁻⁷, 5 metabolites hit). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis recovers MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism (p = 0.00294, 8 compounds including glycine, L-serine, choline, L-threonine) and MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism (p = 0.00739, 6 compounds including glycine, L-serine, adenosine). Driver metabolites glycine (C00037) and L-serine (C00065) are verified members of both the glycine–serine–threonine cluster and the methionine–cysteine module. S-adenosylmethionine (C00019) anchors the methionine/cysteine cluster. Choline (C00114) participates in glycerophospholipid metabolism and glycine–serine metabolism. 3,4-Dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043) is detected in the tyrosine metabolism module (p = 0.048, 3 hits). Adenosine (C00212) links the methionine/cysteine module to purine metabolism via selenoamino acid metabolism.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on amino-acid metabolic pathways as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies KEGG:map00260 Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism as the top hit (FDR = 8.59 × 10⁻¹⁷, fold enrichment 737.4, 7 metabolites hit), with SMPDB Methionine Metabolism (FDR = 1.51 × 10⁻¹⁵, 6 metabolites hit) and KEGG:map00270 Methionine Metabolism (FDR = 1.05 × 10⁻¹⁴, 6 metabolites hit) as strong secondary signals. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00670 One carbon pool by folate (p = 8.36 × 10⁻¹⁰, 6 metabolites hit) and KEGG:hsa00260 Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (p = 3.33 × 10⁻⁷, 5 metabolites hit). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis recovers MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism (p = 0.00294, 8 compounds including glycine, L-serine, choline, L-threonine) and MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism (p = 0.00739, 6 compounds including glycine, L-serine, adenosine). Driver metabolites glycine (C00037) and L-serine (C00065) are verified members of both the glycine–serine–threonine cluster and the methionine–cysteine module. S-adenosylmethionine (C00019) anchors the methionine/cysteine cluster. Choline (C00114) participates in glycerophospholipid metabolism and glycine–serine metabolism. 3,4-Dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043) is detected in the tyrosine metabolism module (p = 0.048, 3 hits). Adenosine (C00212) links the methionine/cysteine module to purine metabolism via selenoamino acid metabolism.
